question: What fish evidence does the 2012-2013 Mindanao LTER survey provide, and what prevents converting its multi-site table into Bangwit species or waterbody rows?

source.citation: Quimpang, V. T., Opiso, E. M., Cudal, M. C., Coquilla, K. L., Buot, G. A., Forten, R. R. C., Bruno, A. G. T., & Amoroso, V. B. (2015). Assessment and Monitoring of Fish Species in the Mountain Streams and Lake of Mindanao LTER Sites. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 6, 100-117. https://doi.org/10.7828/ajob.v6i1.697.
source.access: The publisher-hosted article page and full-text PDF were reviewed. The article page and searchable PDF contain no item-specific license or copyright statement; reuse remains unresolved. No PDF, table, figure, photograph, station coordinate or raw data was copied into the repository.

studyContext.reportedCoverage: Five LTER mountain sites: Mt. Apo, Mt. Hamiguitan, Mt. Kitanglad, Mt. Musuan and Mt. Malindang. Table 1 also has a separate Lake Duminagat column associated with the Mt. Malindang area. Figure 2 names eight river/stream sites, but the table groups stream records by mountain rather than linking each taxon to a named stream.
studyContext.sampleWindow: Table 1 and Figure 3 captions report October 2012 and January-November 2013. The reviewed methods do not provide a more specific event-date crosswalk for each site.
samplingMethods: 2-inch mesh gill net in the lake
studyContext.sampleHandling: The authors state that fish were counted, live fish were released, and voucher specimens were preserved in 10% formalin for laboratory identification. The paper provides no collection accession numbers or repository crosswalk.
studyContext.reportedTotals: The abstract and results report 838 individuals across 34 species, with the results parenthetically saying including five unidentified. Table 1 has one Unidentified row, while the conclusion calls this one unidentified species; the wording does not reconcile whether five refers to specimens, individuals, or another count. Table 1 gives 153, 373, 12, 106, 153 and 41 individuals for its Mt. Apo, Mt. Hamiguitan, Mt. Kitanglad, Mt. Malindang, Mt. Musuan and Lake Duminagat columns respectively; these displayed totals sum to 838.
studyContext.siteResolution: The article says GPS was used to determine station locations, but no numerical station-coordinate list or taxon-to-stream station matrix was found in the reviewed article. A mountain-level presence mark is not a precise river occurrence or river-wide distribution.

consistencyAudit.taxonAndStatusCounts: The paper reports 34 species and says 'including 5 unidentified' in the results; its conclusion separately counts one unidentified species, and Table 1 has one Unidentified row. The source does not reconcile whether five refers to individuals/specimens or the category count. Preserve this as a count-wording discrepancy rather than treating five as unidentified taxon labels.
consistencyAudit.duplicateTableLabel: Table 1 prints Sicyopterus lagocephalus twice with different common-name descriptions and different mountain marks. The source does not explain whether these are duplicate records, distinct forms or an identification issue.
consistencyAudit.sourceNameVariant: The table prints Puntius binutatus (and its listed Barbus binutatus synonym). No taxonomic authority check or specimen re-identification was performed in this source review; the separate nomenclatural cross-check is recorded in national-mindanao-lter-2015-multimountain-fish-taxonomy-crosscheck-20261031.json.
consistencyAudit.siteClaimConflict: The conclusion calls Puntius bantolanensis a commonly occurring fish in all sampling sites, while Table 1 marks it only for Mt. Apo and Mt. Hamiguitan.
consistencyAudit.lakeAndMountainScope: Lake Duminagat has its own Table 1 column and a total of 41 individuals. The authors state that the lake was excluded from the mountain-stream similarity and abundance analysis. Do not merge lake and stream evidence or assign Lake Duminagat taxa to all Mt. Malindang streams.

interpretation.safeSummary: This is a historical research lead covering stream assemblages grouped across five Mindanao LTER mountain sites and a separately tabulated Lake Duminagat sample. It reports 838 total individuals and 34 species, but unresolved unidentified-count wording, duplicate printed name rows, coarse stream locality, and lack of accessible voucher identifiers prevent app admission.
notSupported: A current or complete fish checklist for any mountain, named river, lake or Mindanao region.
Exact species-to-river or species-to-station assignments from the mountain-level presence matrix.
Resolution of the five-unidentified versus one-unidentified totals, the duplicate Sicyopterus lagocephalus rows or the Puntius spelling/site-claim conflicts.
Independent validation of source identifications, endemic/native/introduced labels or voucher identity.
Current water quality, fish safety, natural diet, bait advice, fishing legality or access permissions.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Publisher-hosted full-text primary survey with reported collection methods, broad site groups, table-level totals and a statement that vouchers were preserved. The paper does not provide public voucher accessions, numerical station coordinates or species-to-named-stream links.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: No item-specific reuse license or permission statement was located on the reviewed publisher page or in searchable PDF text. Article, data, map and image reuse is not approved.
qualityAndRights.handling: This review records concise source claims and conflicts only. It does not reproduce the checklist, counts by taxon, maps, images or station coordinates.
qualityAndRights.separateEvidenceLanes: Historical fish collection evidence is kept separate from modern presence, taxonomy, water quality, natural diet, safety and legal/access guidance.

disposition.reason: The source is historical, has unresolved species-count and site-claim conflicts, lacks public voucher/accession details and exact species-to-stream linkage, and has no verified item-specific reuse terms.

nextAction: A targeted nomenclatural cross-check of the conflicting Puntius labels and duplicate Sicyopterus lagocephalus rows is recorded separately. Any broader name normalization must preserve source spellings and remain research-only; next seek public voucher accessions and exact waterbody crosswalks through normal repository access. Keep all results research-only unless identity, site resolution and reuse are separately cleared.

sources.supports: Publisher article metadata, authors, abstract and the link to the full text.
Full-text study methods, sampling periods, reported site groups, table totals, source conflicts and voucher-handling statement.
